name: Tetraneuris

project_scope.note: The local Central Texas perennial concept is Tetraneuris scaposa var. scaposa, taught inside the stable canonical path tetraneuris-scaposa. T. acaulis is an accepted Texas-native species but is a reviewed target-zone FAIL and remains comparison-only.

study_strategy.warning: Do not treat T. acaulis as an equal Central Texas native just because it occurs in Texas. In this project the local perennial rosette/scape learner is T. scaposa var. scaposa; T. linearifolia is the annual comparison.
shared_traits: Low-growing composites with yellow-rayed heads on prominent stalks.
Compare basal foliage and phyllaries, not just head color.

quick_key.if: annual with slender flowering stems and narrow stem leaves
perennial basal rosette with long mostly leafless peduncles and solitary yellow heads
quick_key.then: Tetraneuris scaposa var. scaposa — represented by canonical T. scaposa

quick_key.if: stemless perennial rosette resembling the scaposa architecture but source/location points to Panhandle/Great Plains T. acaulis
quick_key.then: Tetraneuris acaulis — reviewed target-zone FAIL / nonlocal comparison

source_concept_status.learner_action: nonlocal Texas comparison only; no install

source_concept_status.note: Stable canonical path teaches accepted local var. scaposa.

source_concept_status.learner_action: teach inside tetraneuris-scaposa; no duplicate card

look_here_first: Start with the basal leaf cluster, the leafless or nearly leafless flowering stalk, and the head's involucral bracts; compare lower leaves before using ray color.

comparison_cards.title: Fineleaf four-nerve daisy vs four-nerve daisy
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Start at the base, not the yellow flower: annual leafy stems versus a perennial basal rosette with nearly leafless flowering stalks.

field_matrix.linearifolia: Narrow alternate leaves present on slender stems
field_matrix.scaposa: Leaves mostly basal, linear to spatulate; flowering stalks nearly leafless

field_matrix.linearifolia: Solitary yellow head; hairy phyllaries in multiple series
field_matrix.scaposa: Solitary yellow head on long peduncle; outer phyllaries recorded as 8–16

comparison_cards.caution: Pappus counts overlap and are not a reliable stand-alone split. Show the root/caudex and full flowering stem. Color and habitat alone are insufficient.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.need: Matched images of taprooted annual versus perennial caudex and basal rosette; label stem-leaf attachment.
Lower and upper stem plus basal leaves with scale, hairs and gland dots visible.
Side view of outer/inner phyllaries, with arrows at correct bracts.
Mature cypsela and awned pappus scales under macro magnification; use only as supporting character.

overlap_cautions: T. acaulis is a nonlocal reviewed target-zone FAIL; compare its rosette habit without promoting it to a confirmed local native.
T. scaposa var. scaposa is represented by canonical T. scaposa; no duplicate species card.
Yellow ray color and pappus scale counts alone do not separate these species.
